nodes.label: Venue-scan check-in design spec (2026-08-06)
nodes.rationale: Spec only, no production code. The block-architecture admission checklist passes 5 of 6; item 6 (current-milestone critical path) fails because the active phase is Stage 8, so the guardrail's own instruction is 'DEFERRED entry, not code'.

nodes.label: The photograph-and-forward threat
nodes.rationale: A venue QR is only evidence if it cannot be photographed and forwarded. The bar to clear: no check-in without a live accomplice relaying in real time. Real-time relay is not preventable by any QR scheme and is the accepted industry bar. Non-goal: defeating a determined collusive attacker — that is a human-review problem (B8, advisory-only).

nodes.label: Option A — static per-event venue token
nodes.rationale: Smallest cost (one column, one route, one guard) but defeated by a single photograph. Evidentiary value only marginally above the current tap; recommended against for a regulator-facing record.

nodes.label: Option B — rotating QR on a staff door display
nodes.rationale: TOTP in shape: /events/{id}/door regenerates a QR every 30s from a per-event secret plus the time window; the server accepts current + one previous window for clock skew. Highest cost, but a photo is worthless in 30 seconds. Bonus: opened by an authenticated staff member, so the token can carry which staff session was at the door — a candidate fix for the credit_ledger.actor_id gap. Recommended, with C as documented fallback.

nodes.label: Option C — rotating short code, no camera
nodes.rationale: Same rotation machinery as B with no camera permission and no new scan flow. Best accessibility of the three. Practical bar is lower than B's because a short code is far easier to relay by voice or text than a QR.

nodes.label: self_check_in() has no location check of any kind
nodes.rationale: Self-serve check-in was implemented as a tap (ConfirmButton.tsx 'Confirm I'm here'), not a scan. Grepping the repo for geoloc|venue_token|proximity|nfc|beacon returns nothing, so the tap works from anywhere on earth inside the event window. Verified by reading pg_get_functiondef on the live local DB, not from prior docs — the prior doc got this wrong.

nodes.label: checkin_modes.self_serve as kill switch
nodes.rationale: Defaults to {"staff": true, "self_serve": false} and is enforced inside the definer function rather than in the UI. Turning it off disables the path without orphaning any record. Admission-checklist item 4 passes on the existing mechanism with no new work.

nodes.label: New 'venue' value for registrations.check_in_method
nodes.rationale: The CHECK is currently = ANY (ARRAY['qr','manual']), verified via pg_get_constraintdef. A venue scan needs its own value so the ledger can answer 'how was presence witnessed'. Existing 'qr' rows stay ambiguous and should be left alone rather than backfilled. self_check_in gains p_token and a distinct bad_token result code — collapsing result codes into default is precisely the bug fixed on 2026-08-04.

nodes.label: credit_ledger.actor_id attribution gap
nodes.rationale: Currently degrades staff attribution to NULL because it cannot reference a staff actor. A door token carrying the staff session would close it with the same migration.

nodes.label: Re-entry criterion — build after Stage 8
nodes.rationale: Build when Stage 8 closes, or sooner if an accrediting body asks how attendance is witnessed — that question makes the current answer ('we cannot tell you, and the self-serve path had no location check at all') the blocking problem rather than a deferred one. Until then self_serve stays false everywhere, including the demo seed.
